newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar firms to 3-1/2 year high versus yen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar firms to 3-1/2 year high versus yen.

text.p: The dollar extended a move above 115 yen in thin European trading on Friday, its highest level against the Japanese currency in more than three-and-a-half years.

Business was equally quiet on European bourses, though London's blue-chip FTSE stock index did manage to climb briefly to a new record high before the stock exchange closed at the end of a truncated Christmas week trading day.
The dollar moved above 115 yen before European trading began and continued to firm gently during the day to 115.48 yen by 1315 GMT.
It was its first rise to such levels since April 1993 and came after the Japanese currency took a beating after stock prices tumbled in Tokyo this week.

"The weakness of the (Japanese) stock market does emphasise the limited options available to Japanese investors and capital outflows can be expected to continue," Chase Investment Bank said in a daily note.
Chase reckoned that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would probably need to intervene to prevent the dollar/yen breaking much above 115 and that verbal intervention would not work much longer.
"The only question is when the BOJ will step in. Some modest intervention may well be seen soon," Chase said.
The rise by leading London shares to a fresh record, though small in percentage terms, was bolstered by firm bonds and a further advance on Wall Street overnight.
It was short-lived, however, and the FTSE slipped back into modest losses before trading ended at 1230 GMT.
The FTSE rose as high as 4,102.9 before ending down 1.5 points at 4,091.0. Volume was thin, with only 111.7 million shares recorded. Its previous record intraday high of 4,100 was set last Friday.

In London, as with several other European bourses, many dealers extended their two-day Christmas break into the weekend and analysts said market movements were exaggerated because of the thin volumes.
French shares, which had been down in the morning on worries over Wall Street, were flat at midday, having climbed back above the 2,300 level on the main CAC-40 index.
Dealers said trading was thin and fund managers were reluctant to take risks ahead of the expiry of futures and options next Tuesday.
German shares remained in positive territory and ended bourse trade higher, boosted by strength of the dollar around the 1.55-mark level, which is good for German exports.
Dealers said most market players were still on holiday and volumes were thin in the absence of any data to drive significant new gains.
In other currency developments, the Swiss franc continued to suffer at the hands of the mark, hitting three-year lows at 86.68 centimes against a previous 86.20.
And the pound pushed higher amid fresh market thoughts of another near-term rise in six percent British interest rates.
Bank of England Governor Eddie George told a French newspaper this week that he saw further rate rises as necessary at some point.
The pound was trading at $1.6830, up from an early $1.6750 with sterling/mark at 2.6160 against an early 2.6030.
CURRENCIES AT 1315 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5580 marks and 115.48 yen, compared with Tuesday's closing pre-holiday levels of 1.5560 and 114.45.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1315 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares closed down 1.5 points at 4,091.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share was down 3.06 points at 2,300.69.
In Frankfurt the 30-share DAX index closed up 7.31 points at 2,852.88.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $369.55 compared with its London close on Tuesday of $368.65. Silver was at $4.89.
